events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Guam, GU; Rota, MP; Saipan, MP; Tinian, MP
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

A reinvigorated monsoon trough with a potential embedded tropical
disturbance that was previously expected to develop and bring periods
of heavy rainfall to the Marianas beginning Wednesday, has continued
to fallen behind. The mid to long-term model guidance continues to
show a downward trend in any potential cyclogenesis, with the
enhanced monsoon pattern now likely to fall apart over the next few
days, pushing back any potential heavy rainfall into the weekend,
potentially even into early next week as the col overhead lingers and
forces diffusive flow. Due to this uncertainty, this will be the last
Hydrologic Outlook issued for this rain event, unless conditions
warrant a new issuance in the coming days.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
A wet system is currently moving over the southern panhandle through
Monday, bringing an extended period of moderate to heavy rain for
the southern panhandle. Highest rain rates are expected through
early Monday morning, possibly reaching around 0.4 inches per hour
at times, primarily for Ketchikan, Metlakatla, and Misty Fjords. So
far around 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain has been observed in the last 6
hours, with amounts up to 2.25 inches in the surrounding higher
elevations. Rainfall totals could be as high as 2 to 3.5 inches by
Monday afternoon for low elevation sites with up to 4.5 inches in
the higher elevations. Moderate to high confidence for heavy rain
over Annette Island and Ketchikan areas with highest rain totals
near Misty Fjords. Small streams and rivers are starting to some
some rises, but no river flooding is expected at this time. Ponding
of water on some roadways is likely.

An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the following agencies:

Washington Department of Ecology

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Chelan, Douglas, and
Okanogan Counties until further notice due to current and expected
smoke from regional fires. Particulate matter (PM2.5) may reach
Unhealthy levels for areas downwind from active wildfires. Be sure to
check air monitors in your area before outdoor activities.

When air quality is Unhealthy, everyone should reduce exposure.
Limit time outside, avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips
for cleaner indoor air.
